name: Arlington House, The Robert E. Lee Memorial
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Arlington House was built between 1803 and 1818 by George Washington Parke Custis, the grandson of Martha Washington, as a memorial to George Washington. His daughter, Mary Anna Custis, married Robert E. Lee there in 1831, and the couple lived at the estate for 30 years before Lee resigned his U.S. Army commission to join the Confederacy in 1861. Union forces occupied the property early in the Civil War, and in 1864 the grounds were designated as a military cemetery — the origin of Arlington National Cemetery. The mansion was designated a national memorial in 1955 and is managed by the National Park Service in partnership with Arlington National Cemetery.
